deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): X is a topological space and (X_i), i in I, is a family of closed subspaces indexed by a poset I, with X_i ⊂ X_j whenever i ≤ j. This is meant as the combinatorial skeleton of a stratification.

The previous page set up the following:
- X_{Δ0} = ∐_i X_i, with its map to X.
- X_{Δ1} = ∐_{i≤j} Γ_{ij} ⊂ X_{Δ0} × X_{Δ0}, where Γ_{ij} is the graph of the inclusion X_i ↪ X_j.
- Two projections a, b : X_{Δ1} → X_{Δ0}. The map a is a constant étale covering over each X_i with fibre I_i = {j ≥ i}. The map b is a local immersion.

This page makes four points.
1. Identify X_{Δ0} with {(x,i) ∈ X × I | x ∈ X_i}.
2. X_{Δ1} is then the graph of the order relation (x,i) ≤ (y,j) ⇔ x = y and i ≤ j. This is the order induced from the product order on X × I, with X discretely ordered.
3. Hence (X_{Δ0}, X_{Δ1}) is an internal poset in Top, so an internal category in Top:
   - objects X_{Δ0},
   - arrows X_{Δ1},
   - source a and target b,
   - composition given by X_{Δ2} := (X_{Δ1}, b) ×_{X_{Δ0}} (X_{Δ1}, a) → X_{Δ1}. Inside X_{Δ0}^3 this is the set of triples x ≤ y ≤ z, and composition is induced by the projection (x,y,z) ↦ (x,z).
4. The page breaks off at 'Plus généralement, on introduit...'. The next page continues: X_{Δr} = chains x_0 ≤ … ≤ x_r ≅ ∐ over flags i_0 ≤ … ≤ i_r of X_{i_0}. These form a (semi)simplicial space, the nerve of this topological category.

In modern terms, this is the Grothendieck construction (category of elements) of the functor I → Top, i ↦ X_i, viewed as a topological category. Its nerve is the simplicial replacement (Bousfield–Kan / Segal), whose realisation is hocolim_I X_i, mapping to X. In context it serves to encode a stratified space by simplicial/étale-type data, from which the 'stratified topos' (e.g. sheaves on the nerve, or descent data) is to be built.
errors: Minor slip: the object of arrows is written 'X_Δ' (a correction over a crossed-out symbol); it should be X_{Δ1}.

Not an error, but implicit: x ∈ X_i is required in (8). For X_{Δ1} to be closed in X_{Δ0}×X_{Δ0}, as the previous page states, X should be Hausdorff (or the graphs closed); the closedness of the X_i alone does not suffice.

ideas.what: Viewing the I-indexed system of closed subspaces as an internal poset/category in Top, with objects ∐X_i and arrows ∐_{i≤j}X_i
ideas.modern_name: Topological category of elements / Grothendieck construction of a diagram of spaces; Segal's topological category associated to a covering
ideas.usually_credited_to: G. Segal (1968, 'Classifying spaces and spectral sequences'); Bousfield–Kan (1972) for the simplicial replacement
ideas.where_published: Similar internal-category / nerve ideas appear in SGA 4 (hypercoverings, Exp. V bis by Saint-Donat) and in Pursuing Stacks; this specific formulation is not known to be published

ideas.what: Composition defined via the fibre product X_{Δ1} ×_{X_{Δ0}} X_{Δ1} embedded as triples x≤y≤z, projecting to (x,z)
ideas.modern_name: Internal category composition / Segal condition of the nerve
ideas.where_published: FGA / SGA 3 (internal categories and groupoids in a category)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine construction: the nerve of the topological category of elements of a poset-indexed diagram of closed subspaces, which is standard (Segal, Bousfield–Kan). It is interesting only as a step in Grothendieck's unpublished stratified-topos notes, and contains nothing new on this page.
